subject.title: Auto-apply safe doctor fixes on gateway start

question: Should Gateway startup ever apply doctor repairs to persistent config automatically, and if so should it be default-off behind an explicit safe-repair subset rather than broad `doctor --fix`?
rationale: Current source, docs, tests, and issue comments show a deliberate read-only startup boundary plus credible safety counterexamples from unattended doctor repair; automation cannot choose that product/security policy.

options.title: Keep startup read-only
options.body: Leave Gateway startup as validate-and-guide, improve doctor logging and targeted doctor bugs, and keep persistent repair operator-initiated.

options.title: Add opt-in safe startup repair
options.body: Define an allowlisted repair subset with logged diffs, backups, and tests before exposing a named opt-in setting or setup choice.

options.title: Auto-apply safe repairs by default
options.body: Change startup to self-heal by default only after maintainers explicitly accept the compatibility and security risk and require broad upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Keep startup read-only
recommendation.body: Leave Gateway startup as validate-and-guide, improve doctor logging and targeted doctor bugs, and keep persistent repair operator-initiated.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the strongest current routing candidate from recent blame/shortlog across startup validation, doctor flow, and docs surfaces.
